name: The Canyon Sunset
tagline: A stunning tequila and hibiscus pour for golden-hour toasts
desc: Inspired by Utah's breathtaking canyon sunsets. The hibiscus-salted rim and watermelon fade make this the cocktail guests photograph before they sip.
ingredients: Watermelon slice + dehydrated lime to garnish
steps: Salt the rim of a rocks glass with hibiscus salt and fill with ice.
Combine tequila, watermelon juice, lime juice, and agave in a shaker with ice.
Shake vigorously for 12 seconds.
Double-strain into the rimmed glass.
Garnish with a mini watermelon slice and dehydrated lime wheel.
note: For a batch of 20, scale all ingredients × 18 and stir in a pitcher with a large ice block.

name: The Honeymoon Spritz
tagline: Elderflower, lavender, and prosecco — delicate and romantic
desc: Light, floral, and endlessly elegant. This is the cocktail that makes guests say "what IS this?" — and then ask for another immediately.
ingredients: ½ oz Empress 1908 gin (or regular gin)
steps: Add gin, elderflower, lemon, and lavender syrup to a shaker with ice.
Shake lightly for 8 seconds.
Strain into a chilled coupe or wine glass.
Top gently with cold prosecco.
Garnish with a fresh lavender sprig and expressed lemon twist.
note: For a non-alcoholic version, replace gin with seedlip and prosecco with sparkling grape juice.

name: First Dance
tagline: Honey, bourbon, and thyme — warm, bold, unforgettable
desc: Named for that singular moment. The honey-thyme syrup gives this bourbon cocktail a herbal warmth that feels handcrafted and personal.
ingredients: *Simmer 1:1 honey and water with fresh thyme for 10 min, cool, strain
steps: Combine bourbon, lemon juice, honey-thyme syrup, and bitters in a shaker with ice.
Shake hard for 15 seconds.
Strain over one large ice cube in a rocks glass.
Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig lit briefly with a lighter to release aroma.
Serve with a lemon wheel on the rim.
note: Make the honey-thyme syrup up to a week ahead. It also works beautifully as a mocktail base with sparkling water.

name: The Vow
tagline: Rosewater vodka and champagne — pure romance in a glass
desc: Simple, stunning, and deeply romantic. The rosewater and champagne float creates a gradient effect that photographs beautifully.
steps: Combine vodka, rosewater, raspberry liqueur, and lemon in a shaker with ice.
Shake until very cold, about 12 seconds.
Strain into a chilled flute.
Gently float champagne over the back of a spoon to create a layer.
Drop 1–2 dried rose petals on top to finish.
note: This batches beautifully — pre-mix the base and pour champagne to order.

name: Bridal Blush
tagline: Grapefruit, rosé, and lychee — the toast everyone waits for
desc: The pale pink hue and fruity florals make this the most-photographed cocktail we serve at Utah weddings. Crowd-pleasing yet sophisticated.
ingredients: ½ oz lychee juice (from canned lychees)
steps: Combine all ingredients in a shaker with ice.
Shake lightly for 8 seconds.
Fine-strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a lychee on a pick and an expressed grapefruit twist.
note: Make by the pitcher for a pre-reception welcome drink.

name: Provo Garden Party
tagline: Gin, cucumber, and tonic — crisp and effortlessly beautiful
desc: Inspired by the gorgeous garden venues around Provo. Clean, cucumber-forward, and perfect for outdoor summer ceremonies.
steps: Muddle cucumber slices with simple syrup in a tall glass.
Fill with ice.
Add gin and lime juice, stir gently to combine.
Top with cold tonic water.
Garnish with a cucumber ribbon and slapped mint leaves.
note: Use Hendricks or Empress gin for an even more floral profile.

name: Forever Fizz
tagline: Champagne, peach, and vanilla — celebration in every sip
desc: The cocktail for the toast that gets remembered. The vanilla-peach sweetness pairs with dry champagne for a perfectly balanced celebration pour.
ingredients: Top with chilled champagne or Prosecco
steps: Spoon peach purée into the bottom of a chilled flute.
Add vanilla syrup.
Gently pour champagne over the back of a bar spoon.
The purée will bloom upward beautifully — don't stir.
Garnish with a thin peach slice on the rim.
note: This is our most popular welcome-drink or toast cocktail. Batch the purée mixture, then add champagne to order.

name: Salt Lake Sunset
tagline: Aperol, blood orange, and sparkling water over Utah's skyline
desc: The colors of a Salt Lake sunset in a glass. The blood orange and Aperol create a stunning amber-orange gradient that feels uniquely Utah.
steps: Add Aperol, blood orange juice, and lemon to a shaker with ice.
Shake briefly for 6 seconds.
Pour into a large wine glass filled with ice.
Top with sparkling water and stir once.
Garnish with blood orange half-wheel and a small rosemary sprig.
note: Lower ABV option — great for afternoon outdoor receptions.

name: The Adobe
tagline: Bourbon, espresso, and maple — for when work deserves a reward
desc: Our tribute to the team at Adobe Lehi, who demanded something as smart as they are. Espresso intensity balanced by maple sweetness and orange bitters.
steps: Combine bourbon, cooled espresso, maple syrup, and bitters in a shaker with ice.
Shake hard for 15 seconds to fully chill and emulsify.
Double-strain into a chilled coupe or rocks glass over one large cube.
Express an orange peel over the surface and use as garnish.
note: Can be made ahead — batch the bourbon, espresso, and maple, then shake to order.

name: The Quarterly Review
tagline: Gin, cucumber, lemon, honey — sharp decisions, sharper cocktail
desc: Clean, precise, and professional — just like Q3 numbers should be. The cucumber and honey balance gin's sharpness into something effortlessly sophisticated.
ingredients: ¾ oz honey syrup (1:1 honey and water)
steps: Muddle cucumber in shaker tin.
Add gin, lemon, honey syrup, and bitters with ice.
Shake vigorously for 12 seconds.
Double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a cucumber wheel and lemon twist.
note: For non-drinkers: replace gin with seedlip or cucumber water for a mocktail version.

name: Boardroom Whiskey Sour
tagline: The classic elevated — whiskey, lemon, egg white, bitters
desc: The cocktail that closes deals. Silky from the egg white, balanced by lemon, anchored by good whiskey. Universally appealing and endlessly professional.
steps: Combine all ingredients in a shaker WITHOUT ice.
Dry shake hard for 15 seconds to build foam.
Add ice and shake again for another 12 seconds.
Double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Drop 3 drops of Angostura on the foam and drag a toothpick through.
note: The dry-shake step is non-negotiable for the silky foam texture.

name: The Merger
tagline: Two spirits, one glass — tequila and mezcal in perfect harmony
desc: When two great things come together. The tequila brings brightness, mezcal brings depth, and citrus brings everyone to agreement.
steps: Rim a rocks glass with a chili-salt blend and fill with ice.
Combine tequila, mezcal, lime, and agave in a shaker with ice.
Shake for 12 seconds.
Strain into the prepared glass.
Garnish with lime wheel and an expressed orange twist.
note: The chili-salt rim is optional but highly recommended — it becomes a talking point.

name: The Keynote
tagline: Vodka, blackberry, and ginger — bold enough to start a conversation
desc: A cocktail that commands the room. The ginger sharpness and blackberry depth create something memorable without being difficult to order twice.
steps: Add vodka, blackberry purée, lemon juice, and ginger syrup to a shaker with ice.
Shake hard for 12 seconds.
Strain over ice into a highball glass.
Top with cold ginger beer and stir once.
Garnish with 3 fresh blackberries on a pick and a slice of candied ginger.
note: Make blackberry purée by blending fresh or thawed blackberries with a splash of water, then strain.

name: Corner Office
tagline: Mezcal, blood orange, and chili — earned it, now taste it
desc: This is the drink for the people who stay late. Smoky mezcal tempered by sweet blood orange with just enough chili heat to remind you you're alive.
ingredients: Chili powder + blood orange wheel garnish
steps: Rim a rocks glass with chili salt; fill with a large ice cube.
Shake all liquid ingredients with ice for 10 seconds.
Strain into the prepared glass.
Sprinkle a small pinch of chili powder over the surface.
Garnish with a blood orange half-wheel.
note: The smoky-spicy profile makes this perfect for fall and winter corporate events.

name: The Deadline
tagline: Rum, lime, and a lot of sugar — you've earned the sweetness
desc: A riff on a daiquiri built for high-performance evenings. Clean, classic, and impossible to make badly when you start with good rum.
steps: Combine all ingredients in a shaker with plenty of ice.
Shake vigorously for 15 seconds.
Double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Garnish with a lime wheel and serve immediately.
note: The daiquiri is deceptively simple — quality rum and fresh lime are everything here.

name: Virgin Canyon Cooler
tagline: Cucumber, mint, and lime — the most refreshing glass you'll have
desc: This is the mocktail that makes non-drinkers feel celebrated, not accommodated. Clean and vibrant with the cool freshness of a Utah canyon breeze.
steps: Muddle cucumber and mint with simple syrup in a shaker.
Add lime juice and ice; shake lightly for 8 seconds.
Double-strain into a tall glass over fresh ice.
Top with sparkling water.
Garnish with a long cucumber ribbon and a mint bouquet.
note: Add a pinch of Maldon sea salt for a surprising depth of flavor.

name: Desert Rose
tagline: Hibiscus, berry, and honey — as beautiful as it tastes
desc: The hibiscus tea base gives this deep magenta-pink color that photographs like a dream. Sweet, tart, floral, and completely alcohol-free.
ingredients: Dried hibiscus flower + lemon wheel garnish
steps: Brew hibiscus tea double-strength; cool completely.
Combine tea, berry purée, lemon juice, and honey syrup in a shaker with ice.
Shake for 10 seconds.
Strain into a wine glass or coupe over ice.
Top with a small splash of sparkling water.
Garnish with a dried hibiscus flower and lemon wheel.
note: Batch the hibiscus-berry base for parties — add sparkling water to order.

name: The Clean Slate
tagline: Pineapple, coconut, and ginger — tropical and totally guilt-free
desc: Everything you love about a tropical cocktail without the alcohol. The ginger heat balances the sweetness and gives it a grown-up edge.
steps: Combine pineapple juice, coconut water, lime juice, and ginger syrup in a shaker with ice.
Shake briefly for 8 seconds.
Pour into a highball glass over fresh ice.
Top with ginger beer.
Garnish with a pineapple leaf and lime wheel.
note: Use fresh young coconut water if available — the flavor difference is significant.

name: Wildflower Lemonade
tagline: Lavender, berry, and basil — a garden in a glass
desc: Our most popular mocktail at Utah outdoor weddings. The lavender-basil combination is unexpected and elegant in the best possible way.
steps: Muddle basil with lavender syrup in a shaker.
Add lemon juice, berry purée, and ice.
Shake for 10 seconds.
Fine-strain into a glass over ice.
Top with sparkling water.
Garnish with a whole basil leaf and thin lemon round.
note: Make lavender syrup: simmer 1 cup water, 1 cup sugar, and 2 tbsp dried lavender for 10 min. Strain when cool.

name: Mountain Mist
tagline: Apple, cinnamon, and ginger — cozy Utah warmth in cold months
desc: Perfect for fall and winter events. The spiced apple and ginger create a warming, comforting experience that feels festive without being sugary.
ingredients: 3 oz fresh apple juice (or pressed cider)
steps: Combine apple juice, ginger syrup, cinnamon syrup, and lemon in a shaker with ice.
Shake for 10 seconds.
Pour into a rocks glass over ice.
Top with sparkling apple juice.
Garnish with a cinnamon stick and an apple fan.
note: Serve warm in a mug for cold outdoor events — omit the ice and top with warm apple cider.

name: The Nominated Driver
tagline: Watermelon, mint, and lime — the hero of every event
desc: A salute to everyone holding down the car keys. This watermelon mocktail is refreshing enough to make the designated driver the most envied person at the party.
steps: Add mint to a shaker and gently bruise with a muddler — don't shred.
Add watermelon juice, lime juice, and simple syrup with ice.
Shake lightly for 8 seconds.
Strain over fresh ice in a highball glass.
Top with sparkling water.
Garnish with a small watermelon wedge and mint sprig.
note: For a party, blend a whole seedless watermelon with lime juice and strain into a pitcher.

name: Wedding Punch (Serves 50)
tagline: Vodka, prosecco, lemonade, and berry — the crowd-pleasing classic
desc: The recipe Lake Salt has served at hundreds of Utah weddings. Pre-batches effortlessly, scales perfectly, and pleases the entire room.
ingredients: Large ice block or ice ring
Fresh berries, lemon wheels, mint for garnish
steps: Combine vodka, lemon juice, simple syrup, and raspberry liqueur in a large punch bowl or container.
Stir well; taste and adjust sweetness.
Refrigerate base for up to 24 hours.
30 min before service: add a large decorative ice block to the punch bowl.
Pour in chilled prosecco and sparkling water; stir gently.
Float fresh berries, lemon wheels, and mint on top.
Serve with a ladle into punch cups or wine glasses.
note: The large ice block melts slower than cubes, keeping the punch cold without diluting. Freeze fruit inside the ice block for a beautiful effect.

name: Corporate Sangria (Serves 20)
tagline: Red wine, brandy, and fresh citrus — sophisticated and effortless
desc: The go-to for corporate networking events. Make it the morning of, refrigerate all day, and it only gets better. Visually stunning in a clear pitcher.
ingredients: 2 bottles dry red wine (Tempranillo or Garnacha)
1 cup fresh or frozen mixed berries
steps: Combine wine, brandy, orange juice, and simple syrup in a large pitcher.
Add orange and lemon slices and berries.
Stir gently to combine.
Refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours — overnight is ideal.
Before serving, taste and adjust sweetness.
Pour over ice in wine glasses.
Top each glass with fresh mint.
note: Prepare the morning of your event for the best flavor. Add a splash of sparkling water per glass for effervescence.

name: Wasatch Lemonade Stand (Serves 30)
tagline: Lavender lemonade with berry swirl — the mocktail centerpiece
desc: This non-alcoholic batch punch consistently gets more compliments than the alcoholic options. The lavender-berry combination is subtle, sophisticated, and beautiful.
ingredients: 2 liters sparkling water (add just before serving)
Lemon slices, lavender sprigs, and fresh berries for garnish
steps: Combine lemon juice, lavender syrup, berry purée, and still water in a large vessel.
Stir well; taste and adjust — it should be tart, not sweet.
Refrigerate for up to 48 hours.
Just before service, pour into a punch bowl or dispenser over a large ice block.
Add sparkling water and stir gently to preserve bubbles.
Garnish with lemon slices, lavender sprigs, and a handful of fresh berries.
note: Label this clearly as non-alcoholic and watch how many people choose it over the alcoholic options.

name: Summer Celebration Punch (Serves 40)
tagline: Rum, pineapple, mango, and lime — tropical party energy
desc: The punch that turns any corporate summer event into a memory. The tropical base is refreshing and the rum quantity is generous enough to satisfy a crowd.
ingredients: 2 liters ginger ale or sparkling water (add before serving)
Pineapple chunks, lime wheels, mint for garnish
steps: Combine rum, pineapple juice, mango purée, lime juice, and simple syrup in a large container.
Stir well; refrigerate overnight.
Before service, pour base over a large ice block in a punch bowl.
Add ginger ale or sparkling water and stir once gently.
Garnish bowl with pineapple chunks, lime wheels, and mint sprigs.
note: Keep half the batch refrigerated and replenish the bowl every 45 minutes to keep it cold.

name: Utah Spiced Cider Punch (Serves 40)
tagline: Apple, cinnamon, and clove — perfect for fall and winter events
desc: Utah's fall season in a punch bowl. This warming, spiced cider punch is non-alcoholic and beloved by every generation — from the 8-year-olds to the grandparents.
ingredients: Apple slices and cinnamon sticks for garnish
steps: Combine apple cider, cinnamon sticks, cloves, star anise, and orange slices in a large pot.
Simmer gently on low heat for 30 minutes — do not boil.
Add lemon juice; taste and adjust.
Cool completely; strain out whole spices.
Serve warm in a slow cooker OR chill overnight for a cold punch.
For cold punch: add sparkling apple juice before serving; garnish with apple slices and cinnamon sticks.
note: A splash of bourbon or spiced rum per cup makes this easily convertible for adults who want it.

name: The Lake Salt Classic
tagline: Our house signature — the cocktail that started it all
desc: Every bartending brand has a cocktail that defines them. This is ours. The combination of Utah honey, local citrus, and a touch of smoked salt is Lake Salt in a glass.
ingredients: ½ oz Utah wildflower honey syrup
steps: Rim half of a coupe glass with smoked sea salt.
Combine vodka, lemon, honey syrup, and elderflower in a shaker with ice.
Shake hard for 12 seconds.
Double-strain into the prepared coupe.
Express a lemon twist over the surface and perch on the rim.
note: For a unique Utah touch, source local wildflower honey from a farmers market — the flavor is noticeably different and guests always ask about it.

name: The Wasatch Mule
tagline: Utah's answer to the Moscow Mule — sage, ginger, and western spirit
desc: We took the classic mule and gave it a Utah identity. The sage and local honey reflect our landscape, while the ginger keeps the kick you expect.
ingredients: *Simmer equal parts sugar and water with fresh sage for 10 min
steps: Fill a copper mug (or tall glass) with ice.
Add vodka, lime juice, and sage syrup.
Stir briefly to combine.
Top with cold ginger beer.
Garnish with a lime wheel and 2–3 fresh sage leaves.
note: The sage syrup keeps for 2 weeks in the fridge. Try it with bourbon instead of vodka for a Wasatch Mule No. 2.

name: Park City Paloma
tagline: Tequila, grapefruit, and tamarind — the mountain resort cocktail
desc: Park City inspired, globally appreciated. The tamarind rim and fresh grapefruit make this the most complex and reward-rich drink in our rotation.
ingredients: *Mix tamarind paste, chili powder, and salt; rim the glass and let dry
steps: Prepare the tamarind-chili rim and let dry completely.
Fill the rimmed glass with ice.
Shake tequila, grapefruit juice, lime juice, and agave with ice for 10 seconds.
Strain into the prepared glass over ice.
Top with grapefruit sparkling water (Topo Chico Grapefruit is ideal).
Garnish with a grapefruit wedge.
note: The tamarind rim prep can be done the day before. This is our most requested recipe after events.
